question: Does precommitted exact model-height scoring among bounded four-coordinate Hensel digits improve the depth-eight rational model height on the same public relation?
public_hit: the same first eligible public hit pinned in the baseline and short-digit results
derivative_rule: evaluate the exact rational formal parameter t(R) modulo p^(k+1) and its four +p^k coordinate probes; d_i=(t_probe-t_before)/p^k mod p
candidate_rule: find smallest signed-digit radius h<=8 with a linearized cancelling tuple; enumerate every tuple with each digit in [-min(h+2,(p-1)/2),min(h+2,(p-1)/2)] that satisfies the linearized congruence; interpolate A and B before computing any resulting group residual; reject invalid models; choose lexicographic minimum (model_height_bits, maximum_absolute_digit, sum_absolute_digits, signed_digit_tuple)
model_height_bits: maximum numerator or denominator bit length among A,B,x1,y1,x2,y2
controls: retain every admissible tuple and model score; after selecting, verify exact rational curve, both points, R=aP1+bP2, formal parameter, and p-adic depth; independently replay with Fraction arithmetic and brute-force enumeration
comparison: pair depths and exact model bit heights with both previous paths on the same public hit; selection never reads the candidate group residual
stop_rule: exact relation, radius exhaustion, no valid model, modular or exact mismatch, depth 8, or 1200 seconds
claim_boundary: a bounded representation-height selector on one fixed public relation; no relation-yield or end-to-end speed claim
